brief.zh: 换了一批字母：X 是「只有一种笔画」（斜多弯少，或弯多斜少），O 是「两种都多，或者都少」。X 输出大于 0.6，O 小于 0.4。
brief.en: A new batch of letters: X means "only one kind of stroke" (more diagonal than curved, or the other way round), O means "both kinds a lot, or both a little". Above 0.6 for X, below 0.4 for O.

hint.zh: 先试一个神经元，在纸上画画这些点：一条直线分得开吗？神经元的输出，也可以交给另一个神经元。几个神经元一开始的权重一模一样的话，训练能让它们变得不一样吗？
hint.en: Try one neuron first, and sketch the points on paper: can a straight line separate them? A neuron's output can be fed to another neuron. If several neurons start with exactly the same weights, can training ever make them differ?

after.zh: 一条直线怎么摆都分不开异或。两个神经元先各画一条线，把每个点变成两个新的数，输出神经元在新的坐标里一条线就够了：这就是隐藏层。还有一件事：几个神经元一开始完全一样，训练时每一步的变化也一样，永远学不出不同的东西，所以网络的权重要从不同的随机数开始。
after.en: However you place one straight line, it cannot separate exclusive-or. Let two neurons each draw a line first, turning every point into two new numbers, and in these new coordinates the output neuron needs just one line: that is a hidden layer. One more thing: if several neurons start out identical, every training step changes them identically and they can never learn different things. That is why a network's weights start from different random numbers.

t.zh: <level-ref to="4-5"></level-ref>的 X 和 O 在平面上各占一边。这一关换了规则：X 是「只有一种笔画」，O 是「两种都有，或者都没有」。
t.en: <level-ref to="4-5"></level-ref>'s X and O each sat on one side of the plane. This level changes the rule: X means "only one kind of stroke", O means "both kinds, or neither".

t.zh: <level-ref to="4-5"></level-ref>搭的 1 / (1 + e^(−z)) 现在是现成的元件<part-ref to="sigmoid"></part-ref>。
t.en: The 1 / (1 + e^(−z)) you built in <level-ref to="4-5"></level-ref> is now the ready-made part <part-ref to="sigmoid"></part-ref>.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：X 输出大于 0.6，O 小于 0.4。要想的问题：一个神经元是一条分界线，这些点能被一条直线分开吗？
t.en: Your task in this level: above 0.6 for X, below 0.4 for O. Something to think about: one neuron is one dividing line; can these points be split by a straight line?
